'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Israel–Hamas War]]
**[[Humanitarian aid during the Israel–Hamas war]]
***The [[UNRWA]] suspends food distribution in [[Rafah]] due to insecurity and a lack of supplies. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/unrwa-says-food-distribution-rafah-suspended-due-insecurity-2024-05-21/ (Reuters)]
**[[Israeli incursions in the West Bank during the Israel–Hamas war]]
***The [[Israeli Ground Forces|Israeli army]] launches a raid on the city of [[Jenin]] in the West Bank, with sources claiming that seven [[Palestinians]] were killed. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israeli-army-raids-west-banks-jenin-palestinians-say-three-killed-2024-05-21/ (Reuters)]
*[[2024 Iran–Israel conflict]], [[Israel–Hezbollah conflict (2023–present)|Israel–Hezbollah conflict]]
**A high-ranking [[Lebanese Armed Forces|Lebanese army]] officer and three Hezbollah members assassinated in IDF airstrikes in [[Tyre, Lebanon]], [[Beqaa Valley]] and [[Kfar Dajjal]] with three children injured  in a [[school bus]]. The state department of Lebanon issues a formal complaint to the [[United Nations Security Council]].[https://today.lorientlejour.com/article/1414820/students-injured-after-targeted-strike-near-their-school-minibus-in-southern-lebanon-day-230-of-the-gaza-war.html (L'Orient le Jour)]
*[[Nigerian bandit conflict]]
**Gunmen kill 40 people in an attack on a village in [[Nigeria]]'s [[Plateau State]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/gunmen-kill-40-north-central-nigeria-attack-2024-05-21/ (Reuters)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Jenny Erpenbeck]] wins the [[International Booker Prize]] for her novel ''[[Kairos (novel)|Kairos]]'', translated from the German by [[Michael Hofmann]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/books/article/2024/may/21/jenny-erpenbeck-michael-hofmann-win-2024-international-booker-prize-kairos (''The Guardian'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Pixar Animation Studios]] lays off 14% of its workforce, approximately 175 people. [https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/pixar-animation-lay-off-about-14-workforce-2024-05-21/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Singapore Airlines Flight 321]]
**A [[Singapore Airlines]] flight from [[London]], [[England]], to [[Singapore]] makes an [[emergency landing]] at [[Suvarnabhumi Airport]] in [[Bangkok]], [[Thailand]], after experiencing severe [[Clear-air turbulence|air turbulence]] over the [[Bay of Bengal]], resulting in one death and 104 injuries. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c8889d7x8j4o (BBC News)]
*Eleven workers drown after a microbus falls off a ferry into the [[Nile]] River in [[Giza]], [[Egypt]]. [https://english.ahram.org.eg/NewsContent/1/1235/523963/Egypt/Urban--Transport/-women-drown-as-microbus-falls-off-Nile-ferry-in-G.aspx (Al-Ahram)]
*At least five people are killed and 35 are injured as a [[Tornadoes of 2024#May 21 (United States)|strong tornado]] devastates the town of [[Greenfield, Iowa|Greenfield]], [[Iowa]], [[United States]]. A [[Doppler on Wheels]] unit records a wind gust of between {{convert|250|mph|km/h|abbr=on}} and {{convert|290|mph|km/h|abbr=on}} over Greenfield, the strongest winds recorded inside a tornado by a mobile weather radar since the [[2013 El Reno tornado]], equivalent to EF5 intensity on the [[Enhanced Fujita scale]]. [https://apnews.com/article/severe-weather-midwest-iowa-tornadoes-26c73e14ab481ef77a1b0606a2b10adc (AP)] [https://x.com/dowfacility/status/1793317945294094337 (University of Illinois)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Argentina–Spain relations]]
**[[Spain]] permanently recalls its [[ambassador]] from [[Argentina]] amid a diplomatic crisis over [[President of Argentina]] [[Javier Milei]]'s comments about [[Prime Minister of Spain]] [[Pedro Sánchez]]'s wife, [[Begoña Gómez]]. [https://cnnespanol.cnn.com/2024/05/21/espana-retira-embajadora-buenos-aires-argentina-orix/ (CNN)]
*[[Moldova–European Union relations]]
**[[Moldova]] becomes the first non-[[European Union]] (EU) signatory country to sign a security and defense pact with the EU to receive assistance in [[border control|strengthening and managing its borders]], facilitating cooperation in [[computer security|cybersecurity]], and combating [[disinformation]]. [https://www.politico.eu/article/moldova-security-defense-pact-eu-security-cooperation-josep-borrell-border-management-cybersecurity-disinformation/ (''Politico'')]
*A [[Federal Assembly (Switzerland)|Swiss parliamentary]] committee rejects a ruling by the [[European Court of Human Rights]] that alleged the country violated its citizens' [[human rights]] by not doing enough to prevent climate change. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/swiss-parliamentary-committee-rejects-european-climate-ruling-2024-05-21/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Censorship in Israel]]
**The [[Ministry of Communications (Israel)|Israeli Ministry of Communications]] seizes broadcasting equipment from the [[Associated Press]] and suspends their [[Streaming media|live feed]] of [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]], accusing them of breaking the new media law by supplying images to [[Al Jazeera Media Network|Al Jazeera]]. [https://apnews.com/article/live-transmission-israel-associated-press-57e8f662907334ba3599156276381190 (AP)]
*[[Canada|Canadian]] serial killer [[Robert Pickton]] is reported to be on life support after being physically attacked in a prison in [[Port-Cartier]], [[Quebec]]. [https://vancouversun.com/news/crime/bc-serial-killer-robert-pickton-savagely-attacked-in-prison (''Vancouver Sun'')]
*The European Union passes the [[Artificial Intelligence Act]], to be applied in 2026. The act imposes strict transparency obligations on [[artificial intelligence systems integration|AI systems]], restricts governments from using real-time biometric surveillance in public spaces, and bans social scoring, [[predictive policing]], and untargeted scraping of facial images. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/eu-countries-back-landmark-artificial-intelligence-rules-2024-05-21/ (Reuters)]
*A court in [[Saint Petersburg]], [[Russia]], sentences [[Anatoly Maslov]], a 77-year-old hypersonic missiles expert, to 14 years in prison for state [[treason]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russian-hypersonics-expert-jailed-14-years-treason-2024-05-21/ (Reuters)]
*The [[Netherlands]] moves to ban international adoptions. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/netherlands-will-no-longer-allow-international-adoptions-2024-05-21/ (Reuters)]
